prompt:
Create a premium cinematic luxury travel poster for ISTANBUL, TÜRKİYE, designed like an exclusive international tourism campaign. Use a vertical 2:3 poster composition with an elegant editorial travel-magazine feel. Show a romantic historic Istanbul street descending toward the Bosphorus during warm golden sunset, framed by ornate Ottoman-era wooden buildings and elegant stone façades. On the left, include a dark carved wooden café building with balconies, hanging pink bougainvillea, warm lanterns, outdoor café tables, and visible shop signs reading “NİŞANTAŞI KAHVESİ” on both a round hanging sign and an awning. On the right, include a stone spice shop with glowing display shelves, flower boxes, lanterns, and signs reading “HACI ALİ BAHARAT” and “BAHARAT.” The foreground should have a wet-looking cobblestone street with pedestrians walking downhill, small café chairs, potted plants, and warm reflections. In the middle distance, show the Bosphorus water with exactly one classic white-and-red ferry boat crossing from left to right. Across the water, depict Istanbul’s skyline with exactly two monumental mosque complexes, multiple domes, and six slender minarets, with the sun low behind them. The sky should be dramatic and luminous with orange, gold, and peach clouds.

Typography: Large refined serif headline centered near the top reading “ISTANBUL,” on the first line and “TÜRKİYE” on the second line. Place a small Turkish flag to the right of the second line. Beneath the title, add a thin ornamental divider and a graceful cursive tagline reading “Where Two Worlds Meet.” Use black or very dark brown typography with luxurious spacing, high contrast, and a classic tourism-poster hierarchy.

Visual style: ultra-detailed cinematic realism, premium travel poster, warm sunset color grading, atmospheric depth, romantic old-city charm, crisp architectural detail, glowing lantern light, rich flowers, reflective cobblestones, elegant composition, high dynamic range, no watermark, no extra logos, no modern vehicles, no distorted text.
